scenarios.name: Explain unfamiliar parser
scenarios.objective: Use /explain to understand legacy-ish code before editing anything.
examplePrompts: Explain how this parser treats malformed rows and what tradeoffs it makes.
verify: Confirm the explanation mentions blank lines, trimming, and malformed row handling.
scenarios.fallback: Highlight the reduce block and ask: /explain #selection

scenarios.name: Fix a targeted bug
scenarios.objective: Use /fix or a focused natural-language prompt to repair a known bug with minimal change.
examplePrompts: /fix The discount helper is adding the wrong amount after rounding. Make the smallest change that makes the failing tests pass.
Read the failing tests for scenario 2, find the root cause in scenario_2_discount.js, and suggest the smallest safe patch.
verify: Run: cd sample-app && npm run test:2
Confirm the final code no longer adds an extra cent.
scenarios.fallback: Paste the failing assertion from npm run test:2 into Chat and ask for a root-cause-only fix.

scenarios.name: Generate tests for an untested utility
scenarios.objective: Use /tests to generate a first test suite for a utility that currently has no tests.
examplePrompts: Generate node:test coverage for empty input, trimming, optional highlights, and skipped invalid entries in ide_chat_releaseNotes.js.
verify: Create the new test file under sample-app/tests/.
Run only the new tests with node --test <new-test-file>.
scenarios.fallback: Ask Copilot to propose test cases first, then ask it to turn them into node:test tests.

scenarios.name: Use @workspace for multi-file reasoning
scenarios.objective: Use @workspace to trace behavior across scripts, source files, tests, and docs.
scenarios.where: Whole repository, especially scripts/, scenarios/, sample-app/src/, and sample-app/tests/
examplePrompts: @workspace Where do reset behavior, commit safeguards, and sample-app verification commands live in this repo?
@workspace If I want to explain how pricing, validation, and parser behavior are covered in this repo, which files should I show and why?
verify: The answer should cite multiple files, not just one.
The answer should mention both scripts and sample-app files.
scenarios.fallback: Use #file references for README.md, scripts/demo-clean-slate.sh, and sample-app/package.json, then ask the same question.

scenarios.name: Optional customization walkthrough
scenarios.objective: Show how repository instructions shape Copilot Chat responses for this sandbox.
examplePrompts: What repo-level Copilot instructions are active here, and how should they affect your edits?
Using the repository instructions, propose a safe plan for fixing scenario 2 without broad refactors.
verify: The response should mention minimal edits, testing after changes, and avoiding unrelated churn.
scenarios.fallback: Open .github/copilot-instructions.md and ask Chat to summarize the top three instructions it will follow.
